title: Knock sailors prone, not sitting, when a hit shakes the hull
message:
Knock sailors prone, not sitting, when a hit shakes the hull

Study 3.3.3 leaves a sailor who fails the knockdown save prone for two
rounds, but vessel_knockdown_aboard() sat them down, so attacks during the
wait used the sitting penalty instead of the prone one (POS_RECLINING in
fight.c).

title: Let a sleeper neither defend a prize nor hold her bridge
message:
Let a sleeper neither defend a prize nor hold her bridge

Decision D6 calls a hull abandoned when nobody conscious is aboard, but the
check counted anyone above stunned, and sleeping ranks above stunned: a
stopped hull at sea whose only hand was asleep was no prize, and a sleeper
on the bridge blocked claimship and plunder. The abandoned check and both
bridge checks now use AWAKE().

title: Keep a sinking hull's sink timer across a restart
message:
Keep a sinking hull's sink timer across a restart

The sink timer lived only in memory while the hull's damage was saved, so a
restart found her holed on two sides and rolled a fresh 75-150 s (owned) or
1000-1500 s (unowned) countdown: a hull saved a second from going down came
back with a full timer, and repeated restarts could keep her afloat.
ship_runtime_state.sink_ticks (Phase 19) saves the remaining ticks and the
load restores them, so vessel_update_condition() no longer rerolls.

title: Stop a hull dead when she is holed or starts sinking
message:
Stop a hull dead when she is holed or starts sinking

One holed arc made the maximum speed 0, but the helm then shed way at the
class acceleration, so a warship holed at speed 17 sailed on for several
rooms, and a hull holed on two sides kept moving while her sink timer ran.
vessel_update_condition() now zeroes the speed of a sinking hull and of one
holed afloat; a hull aloft with one hole keeps half speed as before.

title: Accept an in-port arrival as the campaign merchant resuming after restart
message:
Accept an in-port arrival as the campaign merchant resuming after restart

A merchant saved inside the port room berths there after the restart
without changing rooms, which failed the gate's position check. When her
first status is under way, the arrival the gate already requires shows
her autopilot resumed.

title: Add a live vessel damage gate and read legacy refits through a statement
message:
Add a live vessel damage gate and read legacy refits through a statement

test_vessel_damage_in_game.sh runs the tactical harness in --damage
mode: Kohdee checks a new warship's S3 condition display, strikes and
rehoists her colors, holes a target on one side (immobile) and then a
second (sinking), is refused gunnery, repair, and salvage aboard her,
and watches her go down on the timer. The harness then requires the
prototype on the S3 armor scale.

The legacy-refit read in the condition conversion now uses a prepared
statement, keeping vessels_db.c within the SQL interpolation baseline.

title: Show hull damage, holes, sinking, colors, and weapons in shipstatus
message:
Show hull damage, holes, sinking, colors, and weapons in shipstatus

shipstatus keeps its four armor lines and adds the structure of each
side, sails, rudder, the holed sides with what they mean (she cannot
move, half speed aloft, or the time left before she goes down), struck
colors, and each weapon as ready, reloading, disabled with its damage,
or destroyed. SHIPSTATUS help follows in both places.

title: Rescale prototype armor and convert saved hulls to the damage model
message:
Rescale prototype armor and convert saved hulls to the damage model

Phase 19 (study 3.3.10): prototype armor is rescaled once by the class
beam armor over the old vedit default, flagged by armor_scale. Runtime
snapshots saved before S3 carry condition_model 0 and are converted once
at load: the class profile at the rescaled armor, refits recomputed, and
each arc, the sails, and the rudder keeping their damage fraction, with
at least 1 structure per arc since the old model had no holes. The
weapon_damage column joins the fresh-install schema.

The content packages now write S3-scale armor with armor_scale = 1, and
their provisioners apply Phase 19 first. Phase 19 ships with a rollback
that returns prototype armor to the old scale, and a verifier.

title: Take only beaten prizes, and let captains strike their colors
message:
Take only beaten prizes, and let captains strike their colors

Decision D6 closes defect L14. claimship and plunder now take only a
beaten prize: a hull with a holed side, one that cannot move, one whose
colors are struck, or one abandoned at sea with nobody conscious aboard
but the claimant; a sinking hull cannot be claimed. Hostile boarding
grapples only a hull making speed 3 or less, or a beaten one. The new
strikecolors command lets the owner or a helm permit holder of an owned,
stopped hull yield: her colors stay down until she gets under way or ten
minutes pass.

title: Hole vessels, sink them on a timer, and float their cargo
message:
Hole vessels, sink them on a timer, and float their cargo

An arc with neither armor nor structure left is holed. One holed arc
leaves the hull dead in the water (an airship aloft keeps half speed);
two start a sink timer: 75-150 s for a player's hull, 1000-1500 s for an
unowned hull so it can be boarded and looted. A sinking hull cannot
move, fire, or be repaired, and drops her autopilot; a hull saved holed
on two sides starts sinking again at boot. When she goes down, half of
each bulk cargo lot floats off as salvage crates that decay after a day
of game time, and shipsalvage hauls them into the hold of a stopped hull
from the helm through the stowage plunder now shares. The old rule that
a hull sinks the moment its total structure is gone is retired: a gutted
hull whose armor holds is crippled, not sinking. Help drops the stale
running-aground paragraph that S2's grounding removal left behind.

title: Resolve vessel hits through the Duris damage model
message:
Resolve vessel hits through the Duris damage model

A hit now runs Duris's per-fragment resolution: each fragment strikes the
sails (warship rigging takes 85%) or the arc facing the shooter,
scattered across the weapon's spread. Armor absorbs first; a hit it
holds stops unless the shot is a confirmed critical (natural 19-20 for
the ballista, confirmed by a second roll), which carries half the damage
into the structure. On a gutted arc one hit in three deflects into
another section and every hit damages a weapon. Weapon damage
accumulates in the slot and in ship_weapons.weapon_damage: a damaged
weapon cannot fire and one at 100 is destroyed. One structural hit in
nine knocks everyone aboard down unless they make a Reflex save (DC 15).
Until S4 seeds the weapon table every weapon resolves as one ballista
bolt, and shiprepair mends weapons (a destroyed one only while
berthed). Bow structure hits no longer tear the rigging; sail hits do.

title: Give vessel classes the Duris hull profiles, arcs, and prices
message:
Give vessel classes the Duris hull profiles, arcs, and prices

Study step S3 begins with the class condition table in the new
vessels_damage.c: each class takes its DurisMUD analog's per-arc armor
and internal structure at the class beam armor, and its sail hit points
(3.3.1). A prototype's armor is its beam armor, now up to 229, and
scales all eight numbers in proportion; vedit new takes the class beam
armor. Arcs follow Duris: fore 320-40 degrees, starboard 40-140, rear
140-220, port 220-320. The shipyard price is the class price times
0.5 + 0.25 * armor / class armor + 0.25 * speed / class speed, so a
default hull costs the class price. Refits are rescaled to Duris
magnitudes (plating and reinforcement +20%, rigging +10% design speed,
at least 1 and at most 30) and each costs a fifth of the class price.

title: Plan study step S3, the damage model
message:
Plan study step S3, the damage model

The vessel study gains a Phase 3 progress section: the branch and tag
state after the S2 merge, the S3 items drawn from 3.3.1, 3.3.3, 3.3.10
and D6, and the interpretations decided while planning (the ballista
profile until S4 weapon rows, the S1 hit roll until S4, unowned hulls as
NPC hulls, the shipsalvage name, and the interim weapon repairs).
